device: Symmetric evanescent directional coupler (2x2), S-bend pulled

topology_reasoning.what_it_is: Two nominally identical single-mode strip waveguides that run straight and far apart at the four ports, are pulled toward each other by mirror-symmetric S-bends, run parallel and close over a short central straight, then separate again through the mirrored S-bends. The silhouette is symmetric about both the horizontal midline and the vertical midline of the frame — the classic 2x2 directional coupler drawn in cross-section-free top view.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: In the central parallel section the two guides are close enough that their evanescent tails overlap. The composite structure supports a symmetric and an antisymmetric supermode with slightly different propagation constants; beating between them transfers power sinusoidally from one guide to the other. Fractional cross-over power is sin^2(kappa * L_eff), where kappa grows roughly exponentially as the gap shrinks and L_eff is the coupling length plus the effective contribution of the adiabatic S-bend approach/exit regions (where the guides are close but not yet parallel). The S-bends must be gentle enough to be adiabatic (no radiation, no higher-order mode excitation) yet short enough to keep the total footprint at 18 um; the drawn bends are very long and shallow, consistent with that requirement. The wide port separation exists so the four ports can be routed away without residual coupling.
function_defining_knobs: coupling_gap_um - edge-to-edge gap in the parallel region; sets kappa (exponential sensitivity). THE dominant knob for splitting ratio.
coupling_length_um - length of the parallel straight section; sets the accumulated phase kappa*L, i.e. the split ratio for a fixed gap.
wg_width_um - guide width; sets mode confinement, hence how far the evanescent tail reaches (kappa) and the single-mode condition.
bend_length_um - S-bend longitudinal extent; sets adiabaticity (loss) and the parasitic coupling accumulated during approach/exit, which adds to the effective coupling length.
input_separation_um - port center-to-center separation at the facets; sets residual port-to-port coupling and the bend offset that the S-bends must span.
straight_in_um - straight lead-in at each facet; with bend_length and coupling_length it sets the total device length, which the fitted values pin to exactly 18.000 um (the footprint spec).

knob_response.honest_reading: The length knob responds EXACTLY: delta_length_um moves 2.455 -> 7.455 (+5.000 for +5.000 um), so the declared knob moves real geometry, not a reported number. The area sub-check fails ONLY at width_um=0.656 because a directional coupler lengthens BOTH guides when the coupling section grows: measured area growth 6.560 um^2 = 2 x 0.656 x 5.0, i.e. exactly twice the single-guide expectation. Re-running with width_um = 2 x wg_width = 1.312 gives area_growth 6.560 vs expected 6.560 and passes=True. The 2x is inherent to the topology, not a defect.
knob_response.lengths_json_semantics: arms = {guide_total_path, guide_path_outside_coupler} for one guide; their difference is the interaction length (the coupler analogue of MZI arm imbalance). A top-vs-bottom arm difference would be identically zero by symmetry and would measure nothing.
